title: Customer Registration Accepts HTML/Script Metacharacters in Name Fields Without Server-Side Sanitization or Rejection (Defense-in-Depth Gap, No Confirmed Rendering Sink)
description: POST https://zakerne.com/api/public/customers/register accepted and stored a firstName value of '<script>alert(1)</script>' without rejecting the input or stripping HTML metacharacters (HTTP 200, {"success":true,"customerId":"CA-F067D0E9","otpRequired":true}). This indicates the backend performs no server-side output-context sanitization/encoding-on-write for this field. Static analysis of the production JS bundle (index-sxBIrYLU.js) found zero application-level usages of React's dangerouslySetInnerHTML (only React-DOM's own internal generic prop-handling code, which is expected framework internals, not app usage), meaning the primary React SPA renders all text content through JSX's default auto-escaping and is very unlikely to execute this payload as script in the customer-facing web app itself. No authenticated tenant/staff session was available in this engagement to observe how this field is rendered in the staff/admin dashboard (client list, appointment views) or in any server-rendered surfaces (transactional emails, SMS templates, PDF receipts generated via the bundled jsPDF library) -- those surfaces were not directly testable and could theoretically use a different rendering path than the SPA (e.g. an HTML email template) where escaping behavior is unverified.
reproduction_steps: 2. Observe HTTP 200 {"success":true,"customerId":"...","otpRequired":true} -- no validation error, payload accepted verbatim

3. Static review of production bundle for a dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink that could render this field unescaped: grep 'dangerouslySetInnerHTML:{__html:' index-sxBIrYLU.js -> 0 application-level matches (only generic React-DOM internals)
impact: No confirmed exploitation path was identified within the scope of this engagement (React's default text-escaping and the absence of any dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink in the client bundle make client-side stored XSS unlikely via the tested SPA). However, the lack of server-side input validation/sanitization on this field is a defense-in-depth gap: if the value is ever consumed by an untested rendering surface (staff/admin dashboard views not reachable without credentials in this engagement, HTML transactional emails, PDF generation, or a future feature) without equivalent escaping, it could become a stored XSS vector against staff/admin users viewing client records -- a materially more sensitive target than the public-facing pages tested here.
remediation: Add server-side input validation on firstName/lastName (and other free-text customer fields) to reject or strip HTML metacharacters, and independently ensure every rendering surface that displays customer-supplied names (staff dashboard, admin panel, email templates, SMS templates, PDF receipts) applies context-appropriate output encoding. Do not rely solely on the frontend framework's default escaping as the only control, since backend-rendered surfaces (emails/PDFs) are not covered by React's JSX escaping.
references: OWASP WSTG-INPV-01: Testing for Reflected Cross Site Scripting
engagement_note: Rated LOW and status 'unconfirmed' specifically because no rendering sink could be exercised in this engagement (no staff/admin/email/PDF access available). Recommend the client's own team check server-rendered surfaces (email/SMS/PDF templates, admin dashboard) directly, since those were out of reach without provided credentials.
